name: The Spider's Perspective (IMX 2026)
why: Multisensory VR as a hunting spider (airflow fans, vibration haptics, spider colour vision) for museums; an academic paper, so left to the HCI batch.

name: The Forest That Breathes Us (Jennifer Abbott, 2024)
why: VR through a Douglas fir, a coyote and a humpback whale with Suzanne Simard; mainly a forest work, better placed in the plants batch.

name: Border Birds (Dries & Bieke Depoorter, 2022)
why: AI detects birds crossing surveillance cameras at disputed borders; IDFA DocLab 2022. About birds seen by machines, not bird perception.

name: We Are Dead Animals (Tote Tiere Maarten, IDFA DocLab 2025)
why: Re-animates roadkill and hunted animals as collectible cards in a virtual paradise; animal as being, not perception.

name: Honeybee VR (Meta Quest)
why: Consumer VR inside a beehive following foragers; developer not identified.

name: Marco Barotti, Swans / Woodpeckers
why: Kinetic animal-like sculptures reacting to environmental data; sensory translation but not animal perception.

name: Terike Haapoja, Community (2007)
why: Thermal-camera video of animal bodies losing heat after death; thermal perception of animal bodies.

name: Blast Theory, Cat Royale (2023)
why: A utopia for cats with a robot arm, designed around cat behaviour; likely in the HCI-animal batch.

name: Rachel Mayeri, Primate Cinema: How to Act Like an Animal (2014)
why: Humans in ape suits learning chimpanzee behaviour; companion to Apes as Family.

name: Becoming Animal (MASS MoCA, 2005)
why: Group exhibition on human-animal boundaries (Mark Dion, Motohiko Odani, Brian Jungen and others); non-XR works, could become a collection.

name: We Are Dead Animals (Tote Tiere Maarten)
why: IDFA DocLab 2025 VR game: revive, eat and recombine photogrammetry-scanned dead animals; closer to mortality than becoming.

name: The Oracle: Ritual for the Future (for humans and non-humans) (Victorine van Alphen)
why: IDFA DocLab 2025 360° ritual where the audience is overtaken by non-human (AI) entities; machine field candidate.

name: Metamorphic (Sensorium: John Fitzgerald, Matthew Niederhauser, Wesley Allsbrook, Elie Zananiri)
why: Sundance 2020 social VR of context-dependent, shape-shifting Quill bodies; not clearly non-human.

name: Marcus Coates, Nature Calendar
why: Design Museum More than Human 2025; Coates' becoming-animal works (Dawn Chorus, Journey to the Lower World) belong to animals-art.

name: Once a Glacier
why: IDFA DocLab 2022 360° glacier piece with motion-capture dance and Indigenous poetry; visual only.

name: Proteus (Ed Key & David Kanaga, 2013)
why: Island exploration where sound responds to the landscape; the player is a disembodied perceiver rather than a nonhuman being.

name: Paper Beast (Pixel Reef / Eric Chahi, 2020)
why: VR ecosystem of paper creatures; player observes and shapes rather than embodies them.

name: Animal Company (Wooster Games, 2023)
why: Social VR scavenging game with Gorilla Tag-style arm locomotion as small animals; derivative of Gorilla Tag.

name: I Am Chameleon (Shift Logic Solutions, 2026)
why: Multiplayer VR hide-and-seek where players paint themselves to blend into surfaces.

name: Spiders (Soaring Roc Studio)
why: VR game where the player appears to be a spider; not verified.

name: Everything is Crab (Odd Dreams Digital, 2026)
why: Animal-evolution roguelite; not yet reviewed.

name: Spirit of the North 2 (Infuse Studio, 2025)
why: Sequel with a fox and a raven companion.

name: Bee Simulator: The Hive (VARSAV, 2025)
why: Sequel to Bee Simulator with colony building.

name: Isopod: A Webbed Spin-off (Sbug Games, 2025)
why: Spin-off where the player is an isopod.

name: Octodad (DePaul University student game, 2010)
why: Original free student version of Octodad.

name: Ecco the Dolphin: Defender of the Future (Appaloosa, 2000)
why: 3D Ecco sequel for Dreamcast with echolocation and a science-fiction story.

name: Hohokum (Honeyslug, 2014)
why: Play as a kite-like, snake-shaped creature; abstract rather than animal.

name: Goat Simulator 3 (Coffee Stain North, 2022)
why: Sequel; adds little beyond the original for this gallery.

name: Lisa Thomas, climate-futures VR environment
why: Listed as a possible interviewee in Augmented Noticing; not researched. It looks like a climate-futures VR scene rather than a becoming.

name: Daniel Steegmann Mangrané, Phantom (Kingdom of all the animals and all the beasts is my name)
why: VR walk through a scanned Atlantic rainforest (2015). You stay a ghostly human observer, so it reads as a counterpoint rather than a becoming.

name: Robert Zhao Renhui — camera-trap works (Seeing Forest, Trying to Remember a Forest)
why: Singapore forest images triggered by animals themselves; possible 'animal as photographer' counterpoint.

name: Eduardo Kac — Essay Concerning Human Understanding (1994)
why: Telematic dialogue between a canary and a philodendron; interspecies but no participant embodiment.

name: Electric South (Cape Town) New Dimensions Lab catalogue
why: Largest African XR programme; project pages were not reachable, no nonhuman-perspective work confirmed.

name: Hiroo Iwata — Media Vehicle / Torus Treadmill
why: Other body-relocation devices by the same artist.

name: Kaohsiung Film Festival 2024 — 尋山 Seeking the Mountain
why: Kaohsiung VR Film Lab original in which the visitor's senses travel through mountain landscapes; director and media not found.

name: Singing Chen: The Clouds Are Two Thousand Meters Up (Venice Immersive 2025)
why: Taiwanese free-roaming VR based on Wu Ming-Yi's story about the clouded leopard and the Rukai origin myth; check whether the visitor ever takes the leopard's body or view.

name: Jooyoung Oh: Young Bird Care Center (2023)
why: Companion work to Kestrel Drone at Busan MoCA Platform 2023, about technology from the viewpoint of fledgling birds.

name: Zheng Mahler: The Twenty-Three Thousand Sexes of Schizophyllum Commune and Other Stories (M+, 2026)
why: AI-animated films in which 38 Lantau mushroom species narrate their own traits; companion to Mushroom Clouds.

name: Musashino Art University: 環世界展 (Umwelt exhibition)
why: Student and researcher exhibition built on Uexküll and Toshitaka Hidaka to let visitors feel how other organisms perceive; may contain individual becoming works.

name: アニマルめがねラボ (Animal Glasses Lab), Kids Design Award 2019
why: Japanese educational VR for children to see through animal vision; needs details and media.

name: Rejane Cantoni & Leonardo Crescenti — SOLO (2010)
why: Borderline: a floor of linked seesaw plates that reproduces a water surface, with each step acting like a stone dropped into it; the body disturbs 'water' but does not become it.

name: Huni Kuin: Yube Baitana (Guilherme Meneses with the Huni Kuin of Rio Jordão, 2016)
why: Brazilian game co-made with the Huni Kuin; twins conceived by the boa Yube inherit her powers. Whether the player actually takes animal form is unverified.

name: Diana Domingues — VRAquarium (2005)
why: Stereoscopic VR/AR installation that immerses the visitor in a real aquarium hybridised with virtual fish; closer to entering a fish world than becoming a fish. Needs media.

name: Sethembile Msezane — Chapungu: The Day Rhodes Fell (2015)
why: Performance in which the artist stood for hours as the Zimbabwe (Chapungu) bird while the Rhodes statue was removed; strong becoming-bird image but no sensory technology.

name: Leeroy New — creature wearables (Aliens of Manila)
why: Filipino artist-designer whose performers wear plastic-waste creature suits; check whether any work frames the wearer as a nonhuman being.

name: Paul Rosero Contreras — Adrift/becoming ocean (2021)
why: Ecuadorian artist; a virtual exhibition app work titled 'becoming ocean' with an iceberg image; description too thin to classify.

name: Interspecifics (Mexico City)
why: Collective that sonifies bioelectrical activity of bacteria and plants with custom 'ontological machines'; perceiving nonhumans rather than perceiving as them.

name: From Alien to Ally (Espositi, Vetere, Bonarini, CHI 2025)
why: Embodying a non-anthropomorphic robot for non-verbal communication; robot field, for machine-cyborg batch.

name: VR Pigeons / Squid Smack (VR games)
why: The only two 'Animal Biomimicry' games in Yu et al. 2026's corpus of 48 animal-avatar VR games; for the games batch.

name: Supernumerary robotic limbs review (Prattichizzo et al. 2021)
why: Survey of wearable extra limbs; corpus overlaps Third Thumb and six-finger work.

name: Asura hands (Kawaguchi et al., RO-MAN 2023)
why: Owning two left hands in VR.

name: Supernumerary hand illusion in AR (Rosa et al. 2021)
why: Embodiment of a third virtual arm in AR teleoperation.

name: Towards Full Body Co-Embodiment of Human and Non-Human Avatars (Podkosova & Brument 2024)
why: Two users share a four-limbed, two-headed non-human avatar.

name: Walking-in-place with a bear avatar (Tanahashi et al., AHs 2026)
why: Posture and gesture congruence for quadrupedal avatars.

name: Hummingbird (Tsoupikova et al., SIGGRAPH 2022 Immersive Pavilion)
why: Live theatre + VR adventure at EVL; unclear whether participants embody hummingbirds.

name: Virtual bat (Waters & Abulula, ICAD 2001)
why: First 'virtual bat' echolocation-in-VR paper; precursor of the 2007 IJHCS article.

name: Jakob Kudsk Steensen — Primal Tourism (2016) and RE-WILDLING (2018)
why: Primal Tourism's camera switches between human, animal and drone movement; RE-WILDLING imagines the reintroduced Hawaiian crow as a sentient flying entity. Both are screen/game works with weak first-person becoming.

name: Studio Above&Below — Meditative Cohabitation (2023), Latent Listening
why: Multispecies bioacoustic screen installations (Brussels biotope; Perth bird chorus seen by AI). Perceptual translation, weaker embodiment.

name: Birdly World (Somniacs, 2024)
why: Global flight edition with portals to micro-experiences as alternate avatars; mostly human-scale sightseeing.

name: Saša Spačal — Meta_bolus (2018)
why: Installation about smelling geosmin from Streptomyces bacteria and antibiotic resistance; scent-based sensing of microbes.

name: Lynette Wallworth — Hidden/Depths
why: UV-torch installation of bioluminescent deep-sea specimens at ArtScience Museum; perceptual but not embodied.

name: Inherent Rights, Vision Rights (Lawrence Paul Yuxweluptun, Banff 1992)
why: Banff VR longhouse with spirit beings; check whether animal spirits are embodied.

name: Bar Code Hotel (Perry Hoberman 1994)
why: Banff/SIGGRAPH VR where barcoded objects act as characters; object-personas, borderline.

name: Mussel Choir / OOZ (Natalie Jeremijenko, Environmental Health Clinic)
why: Mussels as water-quality sensors that 'sing'; human-animal interfaces.

name: BrainPort / tongue display unit (Paul Bach-y-Rita, 1998–2000s)
why: Electrotactile tongue display successor to TVSS; machine-cyborg holds TVSS only.

name: Duncan the Highland Terrier / Sheep|Dog: Trial by Eire (MIT Synthetic Characters 2000)
why: Voice-directed sheepdog installation; similar to AlphaWolf.

name: Teleporting an Unknown State (Eduardo Kac 1996)
why: Web users send light to grow a plant in the dark; collective plant care, not embodiment.

name: Everything (David OReilly, 2017)
why: Game where you can be anything, from animals to objects to planets; likely claimed by the games batch.

name: Body-swapping experiment with an android (Jazbec, Nishio, Ishiguro 2017)
why: Further android body-ownership study on agency.

name: The experience of new sensorimotor contingencies by sensory augmentation (Kaspar et al. 2014)
why: Qualitative study of feelSpace belt users; companion to König 2016.

name: Neosensory Buzz
why: Wristband that turns sound into vibration, commercial successor of the VEST.

name: Madeline Gannon — Mimus
why: Industrial robot that perceives and follows gallery visitors; robot perception made visible.

name: Adam Harvey — CV Dazzle
why: Make-up and hair styles that defeat face detection; seeing oneself through machine vision.

name: Zach Blas — Facial Weaponization Suite
why: Masks against biometric recognition; critique of machine perception.

name: Trevor Paglen — Adversarially Evolved Hallucinations
why: Images generated by adversarial networks trained on symbolic corpora.

name: Sougwen Chung — Drawing Operations
why: Human-robot co-drawing where the robot learns the artist's gesture.

name: Kai Landre — cosmic ray sense
why: Cyborg artist perceiving cosmic rays as sound; talk video only.

name: Grindhouse Wetware — Northstar / Circadia
why: Biohacker implants that add light or sensor functions to the body.

name: Beat (Venice VR Expanded 2020)
why: VR story where the viewer's heartbeat animates a rusted robot; interaction with, not becoming, a robot.

name: ANA Avatar XPRIZE (2018–2022)
why: Global competition for robot avatars that transport presence, sight and touch.

name: Embodied flight with a drone (Cherpillod, Mintchev, Floreano)
why: Earlier EPFL study on immersive drone flight.

name: Being Barbie (van der Hoort, Guterstam, Ehrsson 2011)
why: Owning a doll-sized or giant body changes perceived world size; object/scale embodiment.

name: Things We Could Design (Ron Wakkary, MIT Press 2021)
why: Book on more-than-human, posthuman design of things.

name: Machine Listening collective
why: Research and art on how machines listen to us (Parker, Stern, Dockray).

name: Jakob Kudsk Steensen — The Deep Listener, RE-ANIMATED, Berl-Berl
why: Berlin-based Danish artist; AR/VR works that let you hear Hyde Park species or revisit the extinct Kauaʻi ʻōʻō; site was unreachable during this batch.

name: Wolfgang Buttress — The Hive
why: UK Pavilion, Milan Expo 2015, then Kew: light and sound driven live by vibrations inside a real beehive.

name: Universal Everything — Future You
why: Mirror installation where an evolving machine avatar learns your movements; possible robot-body entry.

name: Alchemy Immersive — Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
why: UK VR series (2020) at insect scale; mostly shows rather than embodies, borderline.

name: Superflux — Refuge for Resurgence / Invocation for Hope
why: UK speculative multispecies installations (collaborators on MLF's HEAL Institute); no embodiment, but a strong more-than-human counterpoint.

name: Presstube / Dpt. — A Colossal Wave co-creators
why: Montreal collaborators on MLF's A Colossal Wave.

name: Mileece I'Anson
why: Sound artist who sonified plant biosignals for Treehugger; own plant-sonification works may fit Becoming Tree.

name: Mite's-eye lichen VR (William Martinez, ASU)
why: Student VR that shows the world of lichens from a mite's perspective.

name: Green Rhythms (Yuting Xue & Elke Reinhuber, TEI 2026)
why: Follow-up to Bend to on symbiotic human-plant interaction; abstract not available to classify.

name: MYCELIUM (Karoline Winzer)
why: Human-circuit installation where touching participants act as a mycelial network; year unclear.

name: Elowan (Harpreet Sareen, MIT Media Lab)
why: Plant-robot hybrid that moves toward light; plant cyborg rather than human perspective (may belong to machine-cyborg batch).

name: Heather Barnett, The Physarum Experiments
why: Long-running collaboration with slime mould (films, TED talk); observational rather than embodied.

name: Saša Spačal, Symbiome / Syncness / Mycophone_emergence
why: Further microbe and fungus biofeedback installations by Spačal.

name: Tosca Terán, Do Mushrooms Dream of Electric Humans? / Myco-Sound Dome / Mycelia in Space
why: Further fungal bio-sonification works listed on the artist's site.

name: Jakob Kudsk Steensen, Terratic Animism (2017)
why: Room-scale VR winter forest; weaker plant perspective.

name: Symbioverse (Nicole Condon-Shih, 2025)
why: AR installation on lichen symbiosis shown in Sympoiesis.

name: Hortum machina, B (Interactive Architecture Lab, UCL)
why: Geodesic mobile garden steered by its plants' electrophysiology; plant agency, unclear human perspective.

name: Špela Petrič, Plant Sex Consultancy
why: Plant-centred design of reproductive augmentations for plants; year not confirmed.

name: Cybroc (Botao Amber Hu)
why: Kinetic artwork of 'cyborg' broccoli exercising for longevity (ISEA 2025, arXiv 2507.21064); plant-machine, but not first-person.

name: EverForest (Botao Amber Hu)
why: Sustainability manifesto from an on-chain artificial life's point of view (HttF 2024, doi 10.1145/3686169.3686209).

name: Jiabao Li — Squid Map, Wings Against the Veil of Light, What makes us most Human is also so Animal
why: Other multispecies works by EchoVision's co-creator; not researched here.

name: Face Jumping (Gorman & Cannizzaro, 2025)
why: Venice Immersive 2025 VR where an aquarium axolotl pulls the viewer into water and through several nonhuman perspectives; multispecies, so left for the animals batch.

name: Planet ∞ (Momoko Seto, 2017)
why: VR short in a ruined world after climate change populated by giant carnivorous tadpoles; perspective and scale not verified.

name: Octopocalypse (Max Sacker & Arite Szadkowski, 2026)
why: Venice Immersive 2026 installation about ocean creatures; octopus batch may want it.

name: Leah Barclay — Ocean Listening / Hydrology
why: Hydrophone projects on the Great Barrier Reef (2016) and an immersive sound environment of aquatic ecosystems; good companions to River Listening.

name: John Luther Adams — Become River (2010)
why: Chamber orchestra work, sibling to Become Ocean; could be added as a river counterpoint.

name: Annea Lockwood — Becoming Air
why: Recent work whose title matches the air sub-category; content not checked.

name: Ursula Biemann — Becoming Earth
why: Exhibition and research platform on Earth systems and Indigenous knowledge; possible earth/deep-time entry.

name: Paul Walde — Requiem for a Glacier (2013)
why: Orchestral performance on the Farnham Glacier in British Columbia; glacier counterpoint.

name: Agnes Meyer-Brandis — Cloud Core Scanner (2009)
why: Artist research on cloud formation in zero gravity; air/weather counterpoint.
